ip_top_stories.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
ip_top_stories.summary: Sony Music is seeking to significantly expand its copyright infringement lawsuit against AI music generator Udio, adding more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its claims. The move substantially broadens the scope of one of the music industry's major legal actions against generative AI audio platforms. The case is closely watched as a test of how copyright law applies to AI-generated music trained on protected works.

ip_top_stories.title: Disney's Copyright Suit Against Chinese AI Developer Advances
ip_top_stories.summary: Disney's copyright infringement lawsuit against a Chinese AI developer has advanced through the courts. The case is part of a broader wave of litigation by major content owners targeting AI companies alleged to have used protected works without authorisation. The progression of the case is significant for how US copyright law may apply to overseas AI developers.

ip_top_stories.title: Seven Questions about CC Signals
ip_top_stories.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines CC Signals, a proposed Creative Commons framework that would allow rights holders to communicate licensing preferences for AI training use of their works. The piece raises key questions about how the system would work in practice, its enforceability, and whether it can meaningfully protect creators while enabling legitimate AI development. The framework is positioned as a potential middle ground between unrestricted AI scraping and blanket prohibitions.

ip_top_stories.title: Artist Sues Copyright Office Over its Refusal to Register His AI-Enhanced Photo
ip_top_stories.summary: An artist has filed a lawsuit against the US Copyright Office after it refused to register a photograph he enhanced using AI tools, raising fundamental questions about where the line falls between human authorship and AI-generated content. The case could have significant implications for how copyright protection applies to works that combine human creativity with AI assistance. It adds to growing litigation pressure on the Copyright Office to clarify its registration standards for AI-involved works.

ip_top_stories.title: Media orgs push back against the relaxation of federal government's stance on AI, copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: Media organisations are pushing back against moves by the US federal government to relax its position on AI and copyright, arguing that looser protections would harm creators and publishers. The opposition reflects mounting industry concern that policy shifts could effectively sanction AI companies' use of copyrighted content without compensation or consent. The story is part of a broader debate over the US government's approach to AI copyright exemptions.

ip_further_links.title: Can you own a voice? Taylor Swift's latest legal move raises big questions for AI and copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Taylor Swift's legal strategy around voice ownership is being examined as a test case for how AI and copyright law may protect — or fail to protect — vocal identity.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI Must Produce Testimony From Musk Case in Copyright Suits
ip_further_links.summary: A court has ordered OpenAI to produce testimony from the Elon Musk case for use in separate copyright infringement proceedings, potentially broadening the evidentiary scope of litigation against the company.

ip_further_links.title: Mind the Gap: States Step in to Address Ownership of AI-Generated Works Amid Federal Uncertainty
ip_further_links.summary: With federal policy on AI-generated works still unsettled, US states are beginning to introduce their own legislation to address questions of ownership and copyright in AI outputs.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: the divergence of the EU and UK
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how the EU and UK are taking increasingly divergent approaches to regulating the intersection of copyright and AI, with implications for rights holders and AI developers operating across both jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence: the UK's pivot towards a new digital replica right
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of proposals for a new UK digital replica right as part of the country's evolving approach to AI and copyright, examining what protection it would offer creators against AI-generated imitations.

ip_further_links.title: Japan eyes rules to regulate AI summaries' 'free riding' on news
ip_further_links.summary: Japan is considering new regulations to address concerns that AI systems are benefiting from news content without payment, as part of a wider global debate on AI and publisher rights.

ip_further_links.title: Matt Comyn urges Australia to resolve AI copyright standoff
ip_further_links.summary: Commonwealth Bank of Australia CEO Matt Comyn has called on the Australian government to resolve the ongoing standoff between AI developers and rights holders over copyright, warning of broader economic consequences if the issue remains unaddressed.

ip_further_links.title: EU Call for Evidence Targets Generative AI's Impact on Copyright
ip_further_links.summary: The EU has launched a call for evidence examining generative AI's impact on copyright, as flagged in a roundup from IPWatchdog, signalling the bloc is gathering data ahead of potential further regulatory action.

ip_further_links.title: James Daunt Looks to Clarify B&N's Position on AI-Generated Books [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: Barnes & Noble CEO James Daunt has moved to clarify the bookseller's stance on stocking AI-generated books, amid growing industry debate about their place in retail.

ip_further_links.title: Can Congress Fill the Cox v. Sony-Sized Hole in Copyright Law?
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of whether Congress can or will act to address the legal uncertainty left by the Cox v. Sony ruling and its implications for copyright liability in the digital and AI era.
